guarantees.claim: sha3_prefix_o is unconditionally assigned before the case statement to '0, ensuring it is never undriven and defaults to 0 when no case or loop assignment fires.
When st is StSw or the default branch, sha3_prefix_o is driven to reg_prefix_i.
guarantees.cond: st == StSw or st not in explicit case items

guarantees.claim: When st is one of {StAppCfg, StAppMsg, StAppOutLen, StAppProcess, StAppWait} and app_id matches an interface index i, sha3_prefix_o is assigned reg_prefix_i if AppCfg[i].PrefixMode is 0, else AppCfg[i].Prefix.
guarantees.cond: st ∈ {StAppCfg, StAppMsg, StAppOutLen, StAppProcess, StAppWait} ∧ ∃i, app_id == i

guarantees.claim: When st is in the app processing states but app_id does not match any i, the loop does not execute an assignment and sha3_prefix_o retains its initial value of '0.
guarantees.cond: st ∈ {StAppCfg, StAppMsg, StAppOutLen, StAppProcess, StAppWait} ∧ ∀i, app_id ≠ i

assumptions.claim: When st is an app processing state, app_id must be a valid interface index (0 ≤ app_id < NumAppIntf) for a configured prefix to be selected.
assumptions.risk: An out-of-range app_id causes sha3_prefix_o to default to 0, leading to an incorrect SHA3 prefix that may silently break data integrity or protocol correctness.

uncertain_points.claim: No error detection or reporting exists for an invalid app_id while in an application state; sha3_prefix_o becomes 0 without any alert.
uncertain_points.cond: st in app state and app_id out of range
uncertain_points.risk: The SHA3 core may process data with a wrong prefix, causing a silent functional failure.
